description: Scam-call demo data: phone scam campaigns, reported scam caller numbers, and call-script evidence. No users. Numbers other than +13464819285 are fictional 555-01xx numbers.

campaigns.title: IRS back-taxes arrest threats
campaigns.tactic_summary: Caller claims to be the IRS or police, says you owe back taxes and will be arrested today unless you pay by gift card or wire.
campaigns.sample_text: This is Officer Daniels with the IRS. You owe $4,820 in back taxes and there is a warrant for your arrest. Pay today with gift cards or wire transfer or we will send deputies.

campaigns.title: Social Security number suspended
campaigns.tactic_summary: Robocall or caller says your Social Security number is suspended for suspicious activity and asks you to confirm it or move money to a safe account.
campaigns.sample_text: Your Social Security number has been suspended due to suspicious activity. Press 1 to speak to an agent. Confirm your number and move your savings to a protected account.

campaigns.title: Fake bank fraud department calls
campaigns.tactic_summary: Caller says they are your bank's fraud team, reports a suspicious charge, and asks for the code just texted to you or to move money to a safe account.
campaigns.sample_text: This is the Chase fraud department. We blocked a $940 charge on your card. To cancel it, read me the six digit code we just sent and confirm your PIN.

campaigns.title: Fake phone carrier calls
campaigns.tactic_summary: Caller claims to be your phone carrier, says someone is moving your number, and asks for the verification code or account PIN.
campaigns.sample_text: This is T-Mobile security. Someone is trying to transfer your phone number. Read me the verification code we just texted so we can stop it.

campaigns.title: Tech support remote access calls
campaigns.tactic_summary: Caller claims to be Microsoft, Apple or your internet provider, says your computer is infected, and asks you to install a remote-access app and pay for a fix.
campaigns.sample_text: This is Microsoft technical support. Your computer is sending us virus alerts. Please install AnyDesk so we can fix it, and there is a $299 service fee.

campaigns.title: Medicare and health benefits calls
campaigns.tactic_summary: Caller offers a new Medicare card, free medical equipment or a benefits refund and asks for your Medicare or Social Security number.
campaigns.sample_text: Hi, I'm calling from Medicare about your new card and a refund you're owed. I just need to verify your Medicare number and date of birth.

campaigns.title: Utility shutoff threats
campaigns.tactic_summary: Caller claims to be the electric or gas company and says power will be cut off within the hour unless you pay now by prepaid card or app.
campaigns.sample_text: This is the electric company disconnection department. Your power will be shut off in 45 minutes for an unpaid balance. Pay $386 now with a prepaid card to stop it.

campaigns.title: Grandchild emergency calls
campaigns.tactic_summary: Someone pretends to be a grandchild or their lawyer, says they were arrested or in an accident, asks for bail money or gift cards, and begs you not to tell anyone.
campaigns.sample_text: Grandma it's me, I was in a car accident and I'm in jail. Please don't tell mom. My lawyer will call you about the bail money, it has to be cash or gift cards.

phrases.value: your social security number has been suspended

call_evidence.text_redacted: Caller said he was from the bank's fraud team, said a large charge was blocked on my card, and asked me to read back the code they just texted and confirm my PIN.
They said my account was compromised and I had to move my savings to a safe account they would set up today, and not to talk to the branch.
Man said he was an IRS officer, I owed back taxes and there was a warrant for my arrest. He said to buy gift cards and read him the numbers to avoid jail.
Recorded message said my Social Security number was suspended for suspicious activity and to press 1. The agent asked me to confirm my full number.
Caller said they were Wells Fargo fraud and needed the verification code from my texts to cancel a Zelle payment I didn't make.
They said they were my phone company and someone was moving my number to a new phone. They wanted the code they just texted me to stop it.
Caller said my computer had a virus and Microsoft detected it. Asked me to install a remote app so they could fix it and pay a service fee.
Woman said she was from Medicare with a new card and a refund for me, and needed my Medicare number and date of birth to send it.
They said my power would be shut off within the hour for an unpaid bill unless I paid right away with a prepaid card from the store.
Young man said he was my grandson, was arrested after an accident and needed bail. He begged me not to tell his mother and said a lawyer would call about gift cards.
Voicemail said there was a legal case against me with the Treasury and to call back immediately before officers come to my house.
